# Command line reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_reference.py from the Typer app. Do not edit by hand:
run `uv run python scripts/generate_reference.py` and commit the result. -->

Every `lakana` command and sub-command, with its arguments and options, in the order
`lakana --help` lists them. The options of the first section go before the command
name, as in `lakana --output json whoami`.

## Options for every command

Usage: `lakana [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--profile` | text | none | Profile to use from the profile file. |
| `--url` | text | none | Override the profile's platform URL. |
| `--output` | one of `table`, `json` | `table` | Output format. Also read from `LAKANA_OUTPUT`. |
| `--verbose` | flag | off | Show tracebacks for unexpected errors. |
| `--version` | flag | off | Show the CLI's version and the instance's, then exit. |

## `lakana load`

Usage: `lakana load [OPTIONS] {file} {table}`

Load FILE into TABLE of the bronze layer, once.

Shows the schema and the row count and asks before it writes. A first load creates the table; later loads replace its rows or, with --write append, add to them, and fail clearly if someone changed the table in between. For anything that should run again, write a Python asset instead.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FILE` | path | required | The local file: CSV, Parquet, Arrow, JSON, NDJSON or a spreadsheet. |
| `TABLE` | text | required | The bronze table; a bare name means bronze.<name>. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--write` | text | `replace` | replace (the default) or append, once the table exists; a first load creates it. |
| `--format` | text | none | The file's format, if the extension doesn't say. |
| `--sheet` | text | none | A spreadsheet's sheet (default: the first). |
| `--header-row` | whole number | `1` | Row of the column names in a CSV or sheet; 0 for none. |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

## `lakana sql`

Usage: `lakana sql [OPTIONS] {query}`

Run SQL and print (or save) the result, or write it into a table.

With `--into T --mode create --expire-after N` the new table expires N days after its last write or read.

A query that stays queued for 3 seconds prints a line on standard error that says why ('Waiting: ...'), and again when the reason changes; the result still goes to standard output only. Nothing is printed about waiting with --output json.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QUERY` | text | required | The SQL, or - to read it from stdin. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--out` | path | none | Write the full result to this file. |
| `--format` | text | none | parquet, csv or arrow (default: from the extension). |
| `--max-rows` | whole number, 0 or more | `50` | Most rows to display. |
| `--timeout` | number | none | Seconds to wait before giving up. |
| `--into` | text | none | Write the result into this table or view instead of printing it. |
| `--mode` | text | none | create, replace, append or view (needs --into). |
| `--incremental-key` | text | none | Append only rows past the target's max of this column. |
| `--evolve-schema` | flag | off | Let the target adopt the result's schema. |
| `--expire-after` | whole number, 1 to 3650 | none | Let the new table expire this many days after its last write or read. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

## `lakana deploy`

Usage: `lakana deploy [OPTIONS] [repo]`

Deploy REPO to an environment; exit 1 if the deploy fails.

In a CI job, LAKANA_OIDC=github or LAKANA_OIDC=gitlab (or LAKANA_OIDC_TOKEN) exchanges the job's OIDC ID token for a one-deploy CI token instead of reading a stored token.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REPO` | text | none | Repository name (default: lakana.yaml's repo:). |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--ref` | text | none | Branch, tag or full SHA. |
| `--dry-run` | flag | off | Validate and diff only. |
| `--no-wait` | flag | off | Print the deploy id and exit. |
| `--timeout` | number | none | Seconds to wait. |

## `lakana search`

Usage: `lakana search [OPTIONS] {TEXT}`

Find tables, columns, labels, descriptions, runs and people that match TEXT.

Matching ignores case and finds TEXT anywhere in a name, label or description. Exact matches come first, then names and labels that start with TEXT, then those that contain it, then descriptions. Texts in a table's main language always match; translated ones in your language (--lang, else your profile's, else the instance's main language), and the matched column shows a translation's language in brackets. A table or column is listed once. Runs are found by the first four or more characters of their id, their job or their repository. A table is also found by the grain its asset header declares, and shows its kind in brackets after its name; a column by the label or description of its declared measure. You see only what you may read. Use --output json for every field.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TEXT` | text | required | What to find; 1 to 200 characters. |
| `--kind` | one of `table`, `column`, `run`, `principal` | none | Only this kind of result. |
| `--model-kind` | one of `fact`, `dimension`, `wide`, `staging` | none | Only tables whose asset header declares this kind; other results are left out. |
| `--limit` | whole number, 1 to 100 | `20` | Most results to show (1 to 100). |
| `--offset` | whole number, 0 or more | `0` | Results to skip, to show the next page. |
| `--lang` | text | none | Match translated labels and descriptions in this language, such as de or fr-CH. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

## `lakana init`

Usage: `lakana init [OPTIONS] [directory]`

Create a Lakana project that deploys unchanged.

Nothing is overwritten: if a file it would write exists, or a folder inside the project is a symbolic link (a write through it could land outside the project), it writes nothing.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DIRECTORY` | path | `.` | Project directory (default: here). |
| `--repo` | text | none | Repository name (default: the directory name). |
| `--sample` / `--no-sample` | flag | none | Write a small sample to build and query (default: yes for a local instance). |
| `--ci-auth` | one of `oidc`, `pat` | `oidc` | How the CI files sign in: oidc exchanges the CI job's ID token, so nothing secret is stored in CI; pat reads a stored Lakana token. |
| `--template` | one of `python`, `ingest-files`, `ingest-sql`, `ingest-rest` | none | Start from a template. python: the sample plus one Python asset, locked with `uv lock` (needs network access and a few more minutes). ingest-files, ingest-sql or ingest-rest: one asset that ingests from a source, instead of the sample. |

## `lakana env`

Usage: `lakana env [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Manage environments.

### `lakana env create`

Usage: `lakana env create [OPTIONS] {name}`

Create environment NAME (with bronze/silver/gold namespaces).

Write the storage root the one way Lakana compares locations: a lower-case scheme (`s3`, not `s3a`), one slash between path segments and none doubled after `file://` (`file:///data`, not `file:////data`), for `file` an absolute path and no host (not `file://data` or `file://localhost/data`), no `.` or `..` segments, no percent escapes and no `*`, `?`, `[` or `]`. One trailing slash is fine. Another spelling is refused, and the message names the one to use. The root of the disk (`file:///`) cannot hold an environment: use a directory, such as `file:///data/lakana`.

Environments may share a root, and one may lie elsewhere in another's (prod at `s3://bucket`, dev at `s3://bucket/dev`). A root at or inside another environment's `managed/`, `raw/`, `artifacts/` or `_artifacts/`, a deleted environment's too, is refused, and so is one whose own such directory would hold another environment's root: the message names that environment and a root to use instead.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--storage-root` | text | required | e.g. file:///data or s3://bucket/lake |
| `--option` | text, repeatable | none | Storage option key=value (repeatable). Values land in shell history; prefer --secret-ref for credentials. |

### `lakana env list`

Usage: `lakana env list [OPTIONS]`

List environments you can see, or with --deleted the deleted ones.

A deleted environment keeps its tables' files until `purge_after` (the server's undo period, 7 days by default); until then `lakana env restore NAME` brings it back.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--deleted` | flag | off | List the deleted environments that can still be restored, and until when. |

### `lakana env get`

Usage: `lakana env get [OPTIONS] {name}`

Show environment NAME.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |

### `lakana env delete`

Usage: `lakana env delete [OPTIONS] {name}`

Delete environment NAME. Its tables' files are kept for the undo period, then deleted.

Within the server's undo period (`LAKANA_TABLES__UNDO_DAYS`, 7 days by default), `lakana env restore NAME` brings the environment back with its tables, their data and their grants. Until then the name stays taken, and `lakana env list --deleted` shows until when. Views and external tables are removed; an external table's files are never deleted. `--purge` skips the period.

Refused (409) while any repository is deployed to it: run `lakana undeploy REPO --env NAME` for each first. Refused while protected.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--purge` | flag | off | Delete the tables' files at the worker's next clean-up instead of after the undo period; the environment cannot be restored then. Also for an environment already deleted. |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |

### `lakana env restore`

Usage: `lakana env restore [OPTIONS] {name}`

Restore the deleted environment NAME, with the tables, data and grants it had.

Works until the end of the undo period that `lakana env list --deleted` shows, and not after `lakana env delete NAME --purge`. A table dropped before the environment was deleted stays dropped; restore it afterwards with `lakana table undrop`. Needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT (deleting the environment revoked the grants given on it, so usually an administrator's).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |

### `lakana env set-storage`

Usage: `lakana env set-storage [OPTIONS] {name}`

Change environment NAME's storage options or credentials secret.

While the environment has a storage secret, changing the options also needs the right to manage secrets in it (the ADMIN role), because an option such as `s3.endpoint` decides where the secret is sent. `--option` replaces all the options, so pass every one the environment should have. Attaching a secret approves the options it has then.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--option` | text, repeatable | none | Storage option key=value (repeatable). Values land in shell history; prefer --secret-ref for credentials. |
| `--secret-ref` | text | none | Secret holding credentials. |

### `lakana env protect`

Usage: `lakana env protect [OPTIONS] {name}`

Protect environment NAME: lock writes down to deployed runs.

A protected environment refuses every write outside runs of the deployed code (SQL, SDK, CLI and Iceberg REST clients alike) whatever the caller's grants; choose the identity a deployed job runs as with `lakana deployments set-run-as`. A holder of MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT can make one audited write with `--break-glass --reason`. It also refuses deletion and storage changes, and runs Python assets only on workers that run tasks in containers (LAKANA_RUN__RUNNER=docker).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |

### `lakana env unprotect`

Usage: `lakana env unprotect [OPTIONS] {name}`

Remove protection from environment NAME.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |

### `lakana env retention`

Usage: `lakana env retention [OPTIONS] {name}`

Show environment NAME's retention, or set it with --days or turn it off with --off.

The retention applies to every managed table in the environment that sets none of its own (`lakana table retention`). Such a table expires N days after its last activity, and never sooner than N days after this command, so turning it on gives every table its full period. Expired tables are dropped by the worker's clean-up and can be restored with `lakana table undrop` during the undo period. Off unless set. Needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; refused for a protected environment, whose tables never expire.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--days` | whole number, 1 to 3650 | none | Tables that set no retention expire N days after their last write or read. |
| `--off` | flag | off | Turn the environment's retention off. |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |

### `lakana env orphaned-locations`

Usage: `lakana env orphaned-locations [OPTIONS] {name}`

List, or with --delete remove, table directories older releases left without a record.

Releases before location records could leave table directories under `managed/` that no table and no record names: tables dropped before the upgrade, creates that failed, environments deleted before their tables could be restored. The worker's clean-up only counts them. Without `--delete` this is a dry run: it lists each directory with its files, size and newest file, and deletes nothing. A directory with a file newer than `--older-than` (30 days by default) is never deleted. `--delete` asks first (`--yes` skips the question), checks every directory again, and keeps one that a table, a create or a dropped table now uses. NAME may be a deleted environment. Needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT on the whole instance (the ADMIN role), because the storage root may be shared. After restoring the catalog from a backup, keep `--older-than` above the backup's age: a table created after the backup has no record either.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--older-than` | text | `30d` | Only directories whose newest file is older than this many days, like 30d. |
| `--delete` | flag | off | Delete the directories listed as old enough. |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |

### `lakana env usage`

Usage: `lakana env usage [OPTIONS] [name]`

Show how much storage environments use, and the size of the workers' caches.

For each environment: its managed tables (the files of their current version), the dropped tables that can still be restored, its artifacts and its code archives. The figures come from the catalog database; the worker measures the tables in its hourly sweep, so a table written since counts as unmeasured until then. Not counted: the files of older table versions that maintenance has not removed yet, external tables, and files nothing names. Needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT on each environment; the workers' caches need it on the instance.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | none | The environment; every environment you manage when left out. |

## `lakana table`

Usage: `lakana table [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Manage tables and load data.

### `lakana table create`

Usage: `lakana table create [OPTIONS] {name}`

Create managed table NAME (namespace.table).

With --expire-after N the table expires N days after its last write or read: the worker's clean-up then drops it, and `lakana table undrop` restores it during the undo period.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--schema` | path | none | JSON file with the column list. |
| `--column` | text, repeatable | none | name:type, ? suffix = nullable (repeatable). Quote a ? spec, e.g. 'region:string?', so the shell doesn't glob it. |
| `--expire-after` | whole number, 1 to 3650 | none | Let the new table expire this many days after its last write or read. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana table create-external`

Usage: `lakana table create-external [OPTIONS] {name}`

Register external table NAME over files under raw/.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--location` | text | required | Pattern under raw/, e.g. raw/orders/*.csv |
| `--format` | text | required | csv, json or parquet |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana table list`

Usage: `lakana table list [OPTIONS] {namespace}`

List the tables in NAMESPACE, or with --dropped the tables dropped from it.

A dropped table keeps its files until `purge_after` (the server's undo period, 7 days by default); until then `lakana table undrop` restores it. A table that its retention lets expire within the server's warning window (7 days by default) shows when, in `expires`. With --model-kind, only the tables whose asset header says `kind: <that kind>`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAMESPACE` | text | required |  |
| `--dropped` | flag | off | List the dropped tables that can still be restored, and until when. |
| `--model-kind` | text | none | Only tables whose asset header declares this kind: fact, dimension, wide or staging. |
| `--lang` | text | none | Show the texts in this language, such as de or fr-CH. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana table get`

Usage: `lakana table get [OPTIONS] {name}`

Show table or view NAME, its columns, and a view's SQL and references.

A table whose first build did not finish, or failed a check, is shown as `not published`; one that keeps the data that failed a check (`on_failure: keep`), as `kept`. A table that its retention lets expire within the server's warning window says when. An artifact is shown with its name and a pointer to `lakana artifact versions list`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--lang` | text | none | Show the texts in this language, such as de or fr-CH. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana table health`

Usage: `lakana table health [OPTIONS] {name}`

Show table NAME's last maintenance, the newest result of each check, and who reads it.

Readers are counted from the queries that succeeded, per person and day. You see them only with the ADMIN role. A Python task's reads of its inputs count too. Use --output json for every field.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--days` | whole number, 1 or more | none | Readers over this many days (up to the server's kept period, 90 by default). |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana table describe`

Usage: `lakana table describe [OPTIONS] {name}`

Describe or label table NAME or one of its columns, or reset its texts.

The texts you set are shown instead of the asset header's `description:` and `label:` (or a translation file's, with `--lang`), and a deploy never replaces them. `--reset` goes back to the project's texts in that language. You need to own the table, or hold the right to drop it.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--column` | text | none | Describe this column instead of the table. |
| `--text` | text | none | The description, up to 4,000 characters. |
| `--label` | text | none | The label: one line, up to 100 characters. |
| `--lang` | text | none | The language you write in, such as fr; without it, the table's main language. |
| `--reset` | flag | off | Remove your description and label, so the project's show again. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana table delete`

Usage: `lakana table delete [OPTIONS] {name}`

Drop table NAME. Its files are kept for the undo period, then deleted.

Within the server's undo period (`LAKANA_TABLES__UNDO_DAYS`, 7 days by default), `lakana table undrop NAME` restores the table with its data and its grants, row filters and column masks. `--purge` skips the period: the worker deletes the files at its next clean-up. An external table's files are never deleted.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--purge` | flag | off | Delete its files at the next clean-up instead; it cannot be restored. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana table undrop`

Usage: `lakana table undrop [OPTIONS] {name}`

Restore the dropped table NAME, with its data, grants, row filters and column masks.

Works until the end of the undo period that `lakana table list NAMESPACE --dropped` shows. Needs the rights to drop and to create tables in the namespace. When NAME was dropped more than once, the newest comes back; restore an older one with `--as`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--as` | text | none | Restore it under this name, when a table of its own name exists now. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana table append`

Usage: `lakana table append [OPTIONS] {name} {file}`

Append FILE (Parquet, CSV or Arrow) to table NAME.

The table's schema is fetched first. A CSV is parsed straight into the table's column types; Parquet and Arrow are cast to them. Nullability is checked too, and a column that doesn't fit fails here, before anything is sent. A CSV must be UTF-8 (a byte order mark is dropped); one in another encoding is refused (exit 8): convert it to UTF-8 and run the command again.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `FILE` | path | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--format` | text | none | parquet, csv or arrow (default: from the extension). |
| `--source` | text, repeatable | none | A table the data came from (repeatable); recorded as lineage. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana table replace`

Usage: `lakana table replace [OPTIONS] {name} {file}`

Replace every row of table NAME with FILE (Parquet, CSV or Arrow).

Without --evolve-schema the file is conformed to the table's columns first, exactly as `table append` does. With it, the file is sent as it is and the table takes its schema. A CSV must be UTF-8 either way, as for `table append`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `FILE` | path | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--format` | text | none | parquet, csv or arrow (default: from the extension). |
| `--evolve-schema` | flag | off | Let the table adopt the file's schema. |
| `--source` | text, repeatable | none | A table the data came from (repeatable); recorded as lineage. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana table merge`

Usage: `lakana table merge [OPTIONS] {name} {file}`

Merge FILE (Parquet, CSV or Arrow) into table NAME on --key.

A row whose key the table has replaces that row; any other row is added; nothing is deleted, all in one snapshot. The file is conformed to the table's columns first, exactly as `table append` does. The file must not repeat a key and no key may be empty. A CSV must be UTF-8 (a byte order mark is dropped); one in another encoding is refused (exit 8).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `FILE` | path | required |  |
| `--key` | text, repeatable | required | A column that identifies a row (repeat it for a key of several columns). |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--format` | text | none | parquet, csv or arrow (default: from the extension). |
| `--source` | text, repeatable | none | A table the data came from (repeatable); recorded as lineage. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana table maintain`

Usage: `lakana table maintain [OPTIONS] {name}`

Expire table NAME's old snapshots, delete its orphaned files, and remove failed-check tags.

A snapshot kept under the tag of a failed check is removed with that tag once it is older than 7 days. A snapshot that a run still in progress needs to set its table back is kept.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--keep-days` | whole number, 0 or more | `7` | Keep snapshots younger than this. |
| `--keep-last` | whole number, 1 or more | `5` | Always keep this many recent snapshots. |
| `--dry-run` | flag | off | Report what would happen; change nothing. |
| `--older-than-hours` | whole number, 1 to 87600 | `72` | Orphaned files younger than this many hours are never deleted (1 to 87600). |
| `--timeout` | number | none | Seconds to wait before giving up. |

### `lakana table lineage`

Usage: `lakana table lineage [OPTIONS] {name}`

Show table NAME's lineage as a tree (or JSON with --output json).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--downstream` | flag | off | Show what NAME feeds, not what feeds it. |
| `--depth` | whole number, 1 to 10 | `3` | Hops to walk. |

### `lakana table references`

Usage: `lakana table references [OPTIONS] {name}`

Show what table NAME's asset header references, and which tables reference it.

These are the references the model declares (`references:` in the asset header), not lineage: lineage is how data flowed, references are what the model says relates. A reference to or from a table you cannot read is counted, never named.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana table retention`

Usage: `lakana table retention [OPTIONS] {name}`

Show when managed table NAME expires, or set it with --days, --on or --never.

An expired table is dropped by the worker's clean-up and can be restored with `lakana table undrop` during the undo period. Its last activity is the later of its last write (or other change) and its last read through Lakana's queries. Tables in a protected environment and tables a deployed project builds never expire.

Without an option this shows the table's retention. The table's owner may set any. Otherwise, making it expire sooner (or at all) needs the right to drop the table; making it expire later, or --never, needs the right to write it.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--days` | whole number, 1 to 3650 | none | Expire N days after the last write or read. |
| `--on` | text | none | Expire on this day (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). |
| `--never` | flag | off | Never expire, whatever the environment says. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana table expiring`

Usage: `lakana table expiring [OPTIONS]`

List the managed tables that their retention lets expire soon, soonest first.

Each row says when, the rule (and whether the table or its environment sets it) and who set it. Keep a table with `lakana table retention NAME --never`, or give it more days.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--within` | text | none | List what expires within this many days, such as 7d (default: the server's warning window, 7 days). |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

## `lakana artifact`

Usage: `lakana artifact [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Manage artifacts: versioned files such as models.

### `lakana artifact upload`

Usage: `lakana artifact upload [OPTIONS] {name} {path}`

Store PATH (a file or a directory) as a new version of artifact NAME (namespace.name).

Everything in a directory is stored, including hidden files such as .env: point the command at a directory that holds only the artifact. Only files the store does not have yet are sent. Links, devices and Windows-unsafe names are refused before anything is sent; the message names the path.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `PATH` | path | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana artifact list`

Usage: `lakana artifact list [OPTIONS]`

List the artifacts you may read, with their current version and size.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace` | text | none | Only this namespace, e.g. models. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana artifact drop`

Usage: `lakana artifact drop [OPTIONS] {name}`

Drop artifact NAME (namespace.name): every version, its files and its grants.

This cannot be undone. The name becomes free; a new artifact of that name starts at version 1. The files are removed inside the request, so an artifact with thousands of files can take minutes; if the server fails part-way, Lakana's periodic clean-up finishes the job. Needs DROP_TABLE on the artifact, which a task never has. In a protected environment pass --break-glass --reason.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana artifact download`

Usage: `lakana artifact download [OPTIONS] {name} {directory}`

Download a version of artifact NAME (namespace.name) into DIRECTORY.

DIRECTORY must not exist, or be empty. The files appear there only when all of them have arrived and match the manifest; if anything goes wrong nothing is left at DIRECTORY (a directory that did not exist is not there, one that existed is empty again) and the message says what to do. An empty directory is never replaced: it keeps its place and its mode, and the files are moved into it at the end. Nothing is written through a link.

The copy is private to you, because the artifact's contents are access-controlled on the server: files are 0600 and directories 0700 (less your umask), nothing is executable. To open the copy to others run `chmod -R a+rX DIR`. (A read-only copy, files 0400 and directories 0500, is what a task gets as its input; remove one with `chmod -R u+w DIR` first.)

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `DIRECTORY` | path | required |  |
| `--version` | whole number, 1 or more | none | The version to download (default: the current one). |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana artifact versions`

Usage: `lakana artifact versions [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Show the versions of an artifact: when each was made, its size, its file count, its digest, and whether it was deleted.

#### `lakana artifact versions list`

Usage: `lakana artifact versions list [OPTIONS] {name}`

List the versions of artifact NAME (namespace.name), newest first.

A deleted version is listed too, with when it was deleted; its bytes are gone. Version numbers can have gaps. If an upload said the server did not confirm its commit, look here for a version with the manifest_sha256 it names.

On a narrow terminal the table leaves out columns, the digest last, and says which; the JSON form always has them all and the whole digest: `lakana --output json artifact versions list NAME`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

#### `lakana artifact versions delete`

Usage: `lakana artifact versions delete [OPTIONS] {name} {version}`

Delete one version of artifact NAME (namespace.name). This cannot be undone.

The version's files are removed from Lakana's storage, except a file another version still has. A bucket that keeps old object versions, and a backup, still have them. The version stays in `versions list`, marked deleted, with who deleted it and when; its number is never reused. The command says how many files it freed and how many it kept, and why: another version has them, an open upload names them, or Lakana's periodic clean-up decides about them (for example for a large version, a manifest the catalog does not know after a restore, a damaged manifest or a storage failure). Needs DROP_TABLE on the artifact, which a task never has. In a protected environment pass --break-glass --reason.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `VERSION` | whole number, 1 or more | required | The version number, from `versions list`. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

### `lakana artifact uploads`

Usage: `lakana artifact uploads [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

List and withdraw uploads that were begun and not finished. `lakana artifact upload` withdraws its own when it fails; use `list` to find one a killed process left behind and `abort` to withdraw it.

#### `lakana artifact uploads list`

Usage: `lakana artifact uploads list [OPTIONS] [name]`

List your own open uploads, newest first: the id, the artifact, when it began and expires.

Only your own: another person's uploads are never listed. An upload that was begun and never finished (after a killed process, a lost connection or a power cut) holds one of its artifact's 16 upload places until it expires, one hour by default. Withdraw one with `lakana artifact uploads abort NAME UPLOAD_ID`. The list does not say how many files an upload has sent.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | none | Only this artifact (namespace.name); every artifact by default. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--limit` | whole number, 1 to 500 | `100` | Uploads per page. |
| `--cursor` | text | none | Continue from a previous page. |
| `--all` | flag | off | Follow every page. |

#### `lakana artifact uploads abort`

Usage: `lakana artifact uploads abort [OPTIONS] {name} {upload_id}`

Withdraw upload UPLOAD_ID of artifact NAME (namespace.name) that was never finished.

`lakana artifact upload` does this by itself when it fails or is interrupted, so you rarely need it. An artifact allows 16 open uploads at once; an abandoned one frees its place when it is withdrawn or after the upload lifetime (one hour by default). Only the person (or service account) that began the upload can withdraw it, and only while it is open. Files it already stored stay until Lakana's periodic clean-up finds that nothing needs them.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `UPLOAD_ID` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

## `lakana query`

Usage: `lakana query [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Submit queries and fetch their results step by step.

### `lakana query list`

Usage: `lakana query list [OPTIONS]`

List the queued and running queries of an environment.

Running queries come first, then queued ones in the order they will be taken, with the reason each waits. You see your own queries; with MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT on the environment, everyone's, and --submitter narrows them to one principal's. The SQL and the error text are not listed: read them with 'lakana query status ID'. A long list prints a "More results" line with the command that shows the next page.

|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--all` | flag | off | Also the queries that ended in the last 24 hours. |
| `--status` | text, repeatable | none | Only queries in this status: queued, running, succeeded, failed or cancelled. Repeat the option or separate the values with commas. An ended status lists the ended queries of the last 24 hours without --all. |
| `--submitter` | text | none | Only the queries this principal submitted. |
| `--limit` | whole number, 1 to 200 | `100` | Most queries to list. |
| `--cursor` | text | none | Continue after the page that printed this cursor. |

### `lakana query submit`

Submit SQL without waiting; prints the query id.

| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana query wait`

Usage: `lakana query wait [OPTIONS] {query_id}`

Wait for a query to finish.

After 3 seconds in the queue, a line on standard error says why the query waits ('Waiting: ...'), and again when the reason changes. Ctrl-C cancels the query, also one of someone else's if you hold MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QUERY_ID` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--timeout` | number | none | Seconds to wait before giving up. |

### `lakana query cancel`

Usage: `lakana query cancel [OPTIONS] {query_id}`

Cancel a queued query, or ask the worker to stop a running one.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QUERY_ID` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana query result`

Usage: `lakana query result [OPTIONS] {query_id}`

Fetch a finished query's result.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QUERY_ID` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--out` | path | none | Write the full result to this file. |

## `lakana grant`

Usage: `lakana grant [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Manage grants.

### `lakana grant create`

Usage: `lakana grant create [OPTIONS]`

Grant a role or action on a securable to a principal or group.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | text | required | INSTANCE, ENVIRONMENT, NAMESPACE or TABLE. |
| `--principal` | text | none | Principal name. |
| `--group` | text | none | Group name. |
| `--role` | text | none | VIEWER, ANALYST, DATA_SCIENTIST, DATA_ENGINEER or ADMIN. |
| `--action` | text | none | A single action, e.g. READ_TABLE. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment. |
| `--ns` | text | none | Namespace (dotted). |
| `--table` | text | none | Table name. |

### `lakana grant list`

Usage: `lakana grant list [OPTIONS]`

List active grants, newest first; without a filter, every grant.

Filters combine. `--principal` and `--group` list the grants made to them (not those a principal has through its groups: `lakana access explain` says that). `--action` lists the grants that give an action, by itself or through a role. `--env`, with `--ns` and `--table`, lists the grants on exactly that object. A long list prints a "More results" line with the command that shows the next page.

The table names who each grant is for in `subject` (`user alice`, `service ci-bot`, `group analysts`); the API sends ids only, so the names cost one request per principal and group until all are found, and a caller that may not list them sees the ids. A column with nothing in it is left out. When the terminal is too narrow the table leaves out `kind`, `namespace`, `table`, `environment` and `action`, in that order, and folds a long `subject` onto more lines, so that the `id` that `grant revoke` needs always stays whole, and a line under the table shows the revoke command; `--output json` always has every field.

A grant of `MANAGE_GRANT`, `MANAGE_GROUP` or `MANAGE_TOKEN` as a single action has the marker `no effect` in a `note` column, which never drops (a narrow terminal leaves out `table` after the others, so that the `id` and the marker stay whole), and a line under the table explains it, followed by the command that revokes each such grant with its whole id (the first five; `--output json` has all of them and carries the full sentence). Revoke such a grant, and give the `ADMIN` role to whoever should keep the ability.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

## `lakana access`

Usage: `lakana access [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Explain who may do what.

### `lakana access explain`

Usage: `lakana access explain [OPTIONS] {principal}`

Show what PRINCIPAL may do on an object, and through which grant, role or group.

One row per action that applies to the object: `allowed` is the answer of the same check the server makes when the principal tries, and `via` names the grants that give it (a role, a single action, or either through a group). You may explain yourself; explaining someone else needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRINCIPAL` | text | required |  |
| `--scope` | text | none | The object: ENV, ENV/NAMESPACE or ENV/NAMESPACE/TABLE. Leave it out for the instance. |

## `lakana secret`

Usage: `lakana secret [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Manage write-only secrets.

### `lakana secret create`

Usage: `lakana secret create [OPTIONS] {name}`

Create secret NAME; its values can never be read back.

Name its use with `--index`, `--repository`, `--connection` or `--own-env` to bind it as it is created; that needs the right to manage secrets, as `secret bind` does. A connection's own secret is usually created with the connection (`lakana connection create ... --password-stdin`).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--value` | text, repeatable | none | key=value (repeatable). Lands in shell history; prefer --values-stdin. |
| `--values-stdin` | flag | off | Read a JSON object of values from stdin (a leading byte order mark is dropped). |
| `--index` | text | none | Bind it to this package index. |
| `--repository` | text | none | Bind it to this repository. |
| `--connection` | text | none | Bind it to this connection; it becomes the secret it uses. |
| `--own-env` | flag | off | Bind it to its environment: storage and webhooks. |

### `lakana secret list`

Usage: `lakana secret list [OPTIONS]`

List secrets (names and metadata only).

`format_version` 1 marks a secret stored in the original format; set it again with `lakana secret rotate` to store it in the current one.

`use` says what a secret may be used for: a package index or a repository (`use_target` names it), or its environment's storage and webhooks. A secret with no use serves its environment only; `lakana secret bind` gives it one.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana secret rotate`

Usage: `lakana secret rotate [OPTIONS] {name}`

Replace secret NAME's values.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--value` | text, repeatable | none | key=value (repeatable). Lands in shell history; prefer --values-stdin. |
| `--values-stdin` | flag | off | Read a JSON object of values from stdin (a leading byte order mark is dropped). |

### `lakana secret bind`

Usage: `lakana secret bind [OPTIONS] {name}`

Bind secret NAME to the one use it may serve; needs the right to manage secrets.

Bound to a connection with `--connection`, the secret becomes the one the connection uses, in the same step; any other secret of that connection is unbound.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--index` | text | none | Bind it to this package index. |
| `--repository` | text | none | Bind it to this repository. |
| `--connection` | text | none | Bind it to this connection; it becomes the secret it uses. |
| `--own-env` | flag | off | Bind it to its environment: storage and webhooks. |

### `lakana secret revoke`

Usage: `lakana secret revoke [OPTIONS] {name}`

Revoke secret NAME.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |

## `lakana connection`

Usage: `lakana connection [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Manage connections: the databases, file stores and APIs assets read from.

### `lakana connection create`

Usage: `lakana connection create [OPTIONS] {name}`

Create connection NAME of kind --kind; needs the right to manage connections.

Give the kind's address and settings options, and its secret one of three ways: `--password-stdin` (stdin becomes the password, token or key the kind takes), `--values-stdin` (a JSON object of several keys), both of which create a secret NAME-connection (NAME-connection-2, -3, ... when a secret holds that name) that only this connection uses; or `--secret` with an existing secret. The values are never shown again. A connection that needs no secret takes none.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--kind` | one of `postgresql`, `mariadb`, `sqlite-file`, `http`, `s3`, `gcs`, `azure`, `directory`, `tcp` | required | The kind of source. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--host` | text | none | postgresql, mariadb, tcp: host name. |
| `--port` | whole number | none | postgresql (5432), mariadb (3306), tcp (required): port. |
| `--database` | text | none | postgresql, mariadb: database name. |
| `--url` | text | none | http: base URL, such as https://api.example.com/v1. |
| `--bucket` | text | none | s3, gcs: bucket. |
| `--region` | text | none | s3: region. |
| `--endpoint` | text | none | s3: https URL (default: https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com). |
| `--account` | text | none | azure: storage account. |
| `--container` | text | none | azure: container. |
| `--root` | text | none | sqlite-file, directory: the worker's ingestion root name. |
| `--path` | text | none | sqlite-file, directory: relative path in the root. |
| `--user` | text | none | postgresql, mariadb: user name. |
| `--tls` | text | none | postgresql, mariadb: verify-full (default), require or disable. |
| `--ca-file` | path | none | postgresql, mariadb, http: PEM file of your CA certificates. |
| `--auth` | text | none | http: none (default), bearer, basic, api_key or oauth2. |
| `--username` | text | none | http (basic): user name. |
| `--api-key-name` | text | none | http (api_key): header or parameter name. |
| `--api-key-in` | text | none | http (api_key): header (default) or query. |
| `--client-id` | text | none | http (oauth2): client id. |
| `--token-url` | text | none | http (oauth2): https URL of the token endpoint. |
| `--scope` | text | none | http (oauth2): scope. |
| `--access-key-id` | text | none | s3: access key id. |
| `--prefix` | text | none | s3, gcs, azure: only objects under this prefix. |
| `--secret` | text | none | Use this existing secret of the environment. |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | off | Read the secret from stdin: the password, token or key the kind takes, less one leading byte order mark and one trailing line ending. |
| `--values-stdin` | flag | off | Read the secret's keys as a JSON object from stdin (a leading byte order mark is dropped). |

### `lakana connection list`

Usage: `lakana connection list [OPTIONS]`

List the connections of an environment, newest first.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana connection show`

Usage: `lakana connection show [OPTIONS] {name}`

Show connection NAME: its address, settings, secret's name and the assets that declare it.

A CA certificate shows as its SHA-256 fingerprint; a secret's values never show.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

### `lakana connection update`

Usage: `lakana connection update [OPTIONS] {name}`

Change connection NAME; only the options given change. Its name and kind never change.

`--password-stdin` or `--values-stdin` sets the connection's own secret again (or creates NAME-connection, or the next free NAME-connection-N, when it has none). A change that could send its secret somewhere new (the address, a weaker --tls, another --ca-file, another --auth or --api-key-in) also needs the right to manage secrets, unless it gives new values in the same command.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--clear` | text, repeatable | none | Remove 'secret' (unbinds it) or a setting, such as ca_certificate. |
| `--host` | text | none | postgresql, mariadb, tcp: host name. |
| `--port` | whole number | none | postgresql (5432), mariadb (3306), tcp (required): port. |
| `--database` | text | none | postgresql, mariadb: database name. |
| `--url` | text | none | http: base URL, such as https://api.example.com/v1. |
| `--bucket` | text | none | s3, gcs: bucket. |
| `--region` | text | none | s3: region. |
| `--endpoint` | text | none | s3: https URL (default: https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com). |
| `--account` | text | none | azure: storage account. |
| `--container` | text | none | azure: container. |
| `--root` | text | none | sqlite-file, directory: the worker's ingestion root name. |
| `--path` | text | none | sqlite-file, directory: relative path in the root. |
| `--user` | text | none | postgresql, mariadb: user name. |
| `--tls` | text | none | postgresql, mariadb: verify-full (default), require or disable. |
| `--ca-file` | path | none | postgresql, mariadb, http: PEM file of your CA certificates. |
| `--auth` | text | none | http: none (default), bearer, basic, api_key or oauth2. |
| `--username` | text | none | http (basic): user name. |
| `--api-key-name` | text | none | http (api_key): header or parameter name. |
| `--api-key-in` | text | none | http (api_key): header (default) or query. |
| `--client-id` | text | none | http (oauth2): client id. |
| `--token-url` | text | none | http (oauth2): https URL of the token endpoint. |
| `--scope` | text | none | http (oauth2): scope. |
| `--access-key-id` | text | none | s3: access key id. |
| `--prefix` | text | none | s3, gcs, azure: only objects under this prefix. |
| `--secret` | text | none | Use this existing secret of the environment. |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | off | Read the secret from stdin: the password, token or key the kind takes, less one leading byte order mark and one trailing line ending. |
| `--values-stdin` | flag | off | Read the secret's keys as a JSON object from stdin (a leading byte order mark is dropped). |

### `lakana connection delete`

Usage: `lakana connection delete [OPTIONS] {name}`

Delete connection NAME; refused while a deployed project version declares it.

Its secret stays in the environment, unbound.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |

### `lakana connection test`

Usage: `lakana connection test [OPTIONS] {name}`

Test connection NAME: a worker checks that its host can be reached.

Prints ``ok: <message>`` or ``<outcome>: <message>`` with what to do next; exits 1 unless the outcome is ``ok``. Waits up to 120 seconds for a worker.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required |  |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--no-wait` | flag | off | Queue the test and print its id; don't wait. |
| `--id` | text | none | Show an earlier test of NAME instead of starting one. |

## `lakana ci-trust`

Let CI jobs (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) deploy with their OIDC ID token, without a stored token.

### `lakana ci-trust create`

Usage: `lakana ci-trust create [OPTIONS]`

Create a CI trust rule.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |

| `--issuer` | text | required | github, gitlab or a configured issuer URL. |

| `--principal` | text | required | The service account the CI job acts as; it needs DEPLOY. |
| `--claim` | text, repeatable | required | NAME=VALUE the ID token's claim must equal exactly (repeatable). Must include repository_id (GitHub) or project_id (GitLab), ref or environment, and how the run was started: event_name or environment (GitHub); ref_protected, pipeline_source or environment (GitLab). |
| `--kind` | text, repeatable | none | deploy (the default) or dry_run; repeat for both. |
| `--start-on-deploy-jobs` | flag | off | Let a deploy under this rule start the project's jobs with on_deploy: true in its environment, as the CI identity (off by default). |

| `--repo` | text | none | Only this repository. |
| `--status` | text, repeatable | none | Only runs in this status: queued, running, succeeded, failed or cancelled. Repeat the option or separate the values with commas. |
| `--trigger` | text, repeatable | none | Only runs started this way: schedule, api, manual or deploy. Repeat the option or separate the values with commas. |
| `--job` | text | none | Only runs of this job. |
| `--since` | text | none | Only runs created at or after this date or time, such as 2026-10-18 or 2026-10-18T09:30:00Z. Without a time zone it is read in yours. |
| `--limit` | whole number, 1 to 200 | none | Most runs to list (default 100). |
| `--cursor` | text | none | Continue after the page that printed this cursor. |

## `lakana scheduler`

Usage: `lakana scheduler [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

The scheduler role.

### `lakana scheduler status`

Usage: `lakana scheduler status [OPTIONS]`

Show the scheduler holder and queue lengths (admin).

## `lakana worker`

Usage: `lakana worker [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

The workers of this instance.

### `lakana worker list`

Usage: `lakana worker list [OPTIONS]`

List the registered workers and what each is doing (admin).

A worker is alive while its heartbeat is recent and lost after that; a lost worker's row stays for an hour, and the query or deploy it held is ended by the scheduler. The column takes is the work the worker takes: all, interactive (ad-hoc queries) or pipeline (deploys, pipeline tasks and table maintenance). The column caches is the disk its caches take, as it last measured them (hourly).

## `lakana job`

Usage: `lakana job [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Jobs: named selections of a project, started by hand, by the API, by a schedule or after each deploy.

### `lakana job list`

Usage: `lakana job list [OPTIONS]`

List the jobs of the deployed projects: state, triggers, next run and last run.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--repo` | text | none | Repository name (default: lakana.yaml's repo:). |

### `lakana job show`

Usage: `lakana job show [OPTIONS] {name}`

Show job NAME: its state, its triggers with the next run, and its last run.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required | The job's name, as in lakana.yaml. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--repo` | text | none | Repository name (default: lakana.yaml's repo:). |

### `lakana job run`

Usage: `lakana job run [OPTIONS] {name}`

Start job NAME now; if its project is busy, the start waits and begins when it is free.

Exit 0 when the run succeeds, 1 when it fails, is cancelled or the timeout elapses. When the start waits, the command prints what it waits for and exits 0: that means accepted, not run; a script that needs the result follows the run it names with `lakana runs show`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required | The job's name, as in lakana.yaml. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--repo` | text | none | Repository name (default: lakana.yaml's repo:). |
| `--no-wait` | flag | off | Print the run id and exit. |
| `--timeout` | number | none | Seconds to wait. |

### `lakana job pause`

Usage: `lakana job pause [OPTIONS] {name}`

Pause job NAME's schedule; a waiting start still happens and a start by hand still works.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required | The job's name, as in lakana.yaml. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--repo` | text | none | Repository name (default: lakana.yaml's repo:). |

### `lakana job resume`

Usage: `lakana job resume [OPTIONS] {name}`

Resume job NAME's schedule from now; the times missed while paused do not fire.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required | The job's name, as in lakana.yaml. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--repo` | text | none | Repository name (default: lakana.yaml's repo:). |

### `lakana job notify-test`

Usage: `lakana job notify-test [OPTIONS] {name}`

Send a test message to job NAME's webhook and wait up to 30 seconds for the result.

The message carries clearly fake run data. Exit 0 when it was delivered; 1 when the webhook refused it or was not reached (the reason is printed), and also 1 when it is still being tried after the wait (look later with `lakana job notification`). Needs the deploy right.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | text | required | The job's name, as in lakana.yaml. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--repo` | text | none | Repository name (default: lakana.yaml's repo:). |

### `lakana job notification`

Usage: `lakana job notification [OPTIONS] {delivery_id}`

Show one notification delivery, such as the one `job notify-test` queued.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DELIVERY_ID` | text | required | The delivery id `job notify-test` printed. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

## `lakana check`

Usage: `lakana check [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Data quality checks: the results of the checks a run made.

### `lakana check list`

Usage: `lakana check list [OPTIONS]`

List check results, newest first. With --run, the results of one run.

The run column shows 8 characters of the run id; --output json has the whole id.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--run` | text | none | Only the results of this run. |
| `--table` | text | none | Only this table's (namespace.table). |
| `--limit` | whole number, 1 to 1000 | `50` | Most results to list. |

### `lakana check rows`

Usage: `lakana check rows [OPTIONS] {RUN} {CHECK}`

Show the rows a check found in a run.

These are the rows this check found in that run, as they were then, also after the table was set back.

It runs as a query of yours, under your own rights, row filters and column masks: you see the rows the check found that you may read, and every other table the check's SQL reads is read as it is now. It needs the right to read the run and to submit queries, and the right to read every table the check's SQL reads: without it, the command refuses and shows neither rows nor SQL.

The rows stay readable for seven days after a failed blocking check; then `lakana table maintain` removes the snapshot, and the number of rows remains in `lakana check list`. A check that read no snapshot (a view, or SQL that does not read its table) has no rows to show; the message says where to run its SQL yourself.

Prints a table like `lakana sql`; --out writes every row to a file instead.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RUN` | text | required | The whole run id, as `lakana runs list` shows it. |
| `CHECK` | text | required | The check, as `lakana check list` shows it: table/check. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--out` | path | none | Write the full result to this file. |
| `--format` | text | none | parquet, csv or arrow (default: from the extension). |
| `--max-rows` | whole number, 0 or more | `50` | Most rows to display. |
| `--timeout` | number | none | Seconds to wait before giving up. |

## `lakana audit`

Usage: `lakana audit [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Read the audit log.

### `lakana audit list`

Usage: `lakana audit list [OPTIONS]`

List audit events, newest first.

`--output json` shows each event's `detail`. Query text and column values in someone else's events are hidden unless you hold READ_QUERY_TEXT: a query's SQL text shows as its SHA-256 and length, an incremental write's watermark as {"hidden": true}. Your own events show in full. A page that shows other people's events, or `--principal-id` of someone else, is itself recorded in the audit log (ACTIVITY_VIEWED).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--event-type` | text | none | e.g. GRANT_CREATED |
| `--kind` | one of `connection` | none | Only events of this kind: connection is every CONNECTION_*. |
| `--env` | text | none | Only this environment. |
| `--principal-id` | text | none | Only this principal's events. |
| `--since` | text | none | ISO 8601; UTC if no offset. |
| `--until` | text | none | ISO 8601; UTC if no offset. |
| `--limit` | whole number, 1 to 500 | `100` | Events per page. |
| `--cursor` | text | none | Continue from a previous page. |
| `--all` | flag | off | Follow every page. |

## `lakana server`

Usage: `lakana server [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Run Lakana on this machine (local only).

### `lakana server start`

Usage: `lakana server start [OPTIONS]`

Start Lakana on this machine: migrate, then the server and worker.

Stop it with Ctrl-C, or from another terminal with 'lakana server stop'.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--local` | flag | off | Run this machine's own instance. |
| `--data-dir` | path | none | Data directory (default: XDG). |
| `--port` | whole number | `8765` | Port to bind on 127.0.0.1 (default 8765). |
| `--log-requests` | flag | off | Print a line for every request the server answers (default: none). |

### `lakana server status`

Usage: `lakana server status [OPTIONS]`

Report whether a local-mode instance is running.

Running means the data directory's lock is held (even before any pidfile exists, or while `/healthz` is slow), or the recorded server PID is alive and answers `/healthz`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` | path | none | Data directory (default: XDG). |

### `lakana server stop`

Usage: `lakana server stop [OPTIONS]`

Stop this machine's local instance, as Ctrl-C in its terminal does.

Asks the instance in the data directory to shut down and waits up to 30 seconds for it to leave. Nothing running is not an error. It stops only the instance on this machine: a Compose stack stops with 'docker compose down' in its bundle directory.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--data-dir` | path | none | Data directory (default: XDG). |

### `lakana server reset`

Usage: `lakana server reset [OPTIONS]`

Delete this machine's local instance's data, so the next start is a first run.

Deletes the database, the tables' files and the secrets key of the instance in the data directory, and nothing else: your project files are never touched. It refuses while the instance runs, and in any directory that is not a local instance's data directory.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--local` | flag | off | Reset this machine's own instance. |
| `--data-dir` | path | none | Data directory (default: XDG). |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |
